title: Bulla registry
description: The shape of registry.json, which every consumer depends on. scripts/consolidate.ts checks each consolidation against it before writing, so a run that breaks the shape or drops a required field fails before anything is committed. Rules JSON Schema can't express (network keys match chainId, pools reference known networks and clients, logo files exist, unique pool addresses) are checked in scripts/validate-registry.ts. The pool and client definitions copy factoring-contracts' pools.schema.json on purpose: a change upstream must also change this file, so it gets reviewed here.

networks.description: Keyed by chain ID as a decimal string.

clients.description: Keyed by client key, e.g. tcs. A client is who a factoring pool factors invoices for; one client can have many pools. From factoring-contracts' pools.json.

pools.description: Every factoring pool on every chain, archived ones included. From factoring-contracts' pools.json.

slug.description: The network's name in the subgraph (bulla-contracts-<slug>) and in pools.json.

network.description: wrappedNativeToken is the ERC-20 that wraps the native currency 1:1 (WETH on Ethereum), or the native currency's own ERC-20 where it is one (CELO on Celo). usdc is Circle's native USDC, or the official bridged USDC where there is none (its symbol says which, e.g. USDC.e).

contracts.description: Keyed by source repo, then contract name.

subgraphEndpoints.description: One endpoint per Goldsky tag: dev for the dev stage, prod for production. They are constant (the network slug plus a fixed tag) and change only when a network is added; which build a tag serves is set by tagging in the subgraph repo.

nativeCurrency.description: The network's own currency, which pays for gas and has no contract (Bulla uses the zero address for it).

token.description: An ERC-20 token. symbol and decimals are what the contract returns.

logo.description: An https URL, or a path relative to registry.json (e.g. factoring-contracts/logos/tcs.png). Absent: show the Bulla logo.

category.description: Where the app lists the pool. active: live. test: a test pool, on the Test tab. archived: no longer in use but still resolves. hidden: on no tab, and its details page shows nothing of it, e.g. a pool superseded by a redeploy.

shareToken.description: The pool's own ERC-20 share token. Its address is the pool address.

asset.description: The underlying asset the pool takes deposits in and funds invoices with.

redeem.description: Absent on V0 and V1 pools, which have no redeem permissions; present from V2.1 on.

insuranceBps.description: Absent before V2.2, which has no insurance fee; present on every V2.2 pool.

address.description: The pool contract, which is also its share token.

client.description: A key of clients. Separate from poolKey: tcs-wyoming is client tcs.

poolKey.description: The name factoring-contracts' deploy scripts take, e.g. tcs-wyoming. A redeploy keeps the poolKey, so several pools on a chain can share one, but only one of them is current (no supersededBy). Only pools those scripts manage have one.

supersededBy.description: The pool on the same chain that replaced this one when it was redeployed.

deployBlock.description: The block that created the pool; the subgraph's start block for it.
